Declare a compositional variable

Source: R/declare_composition.R
declare_composition.Rd

Builds a compD object from a set of composition parts. It validates the parts (zeroes permitted), summarizes zero occurrence, imputes any zeroes, optionally flags compositional outliers and stores the closed composition.

Usage

declare_composition(
  data,
  parts,
  closure = 1,
  labels = NULL,
  units = NULL,
  impute_method = "lrEM",
  detect_outliers = FALSE,
  outlier_args = list(),
  ...
)

Arguments

data

A data frame containing the composition parts.

parts

Character vector of column names making up the composition (at least two parts). Required; there is no default.

closure

Scale the composition is reported on. Either a positive number (e.g., 1440 for minutes-per-day, 1 for proportions) or one of the strings "percent" (equivalent to closure = 100) or "mean" (the average of the observed row totals of the original input parts). The resolved numeric value is stored as compD$closure, and every downstream summary, plot and prediction uses it. Defaults to 1 (unit proportions).

labels

Optional display labels for the parts, reported in summary and plot output in place of the raw part names. Either a named character vector mapping part names to labels (e.g., c(MVPA = "Exercise (min/day)"); parts not named keep their raw name) or an unnamed character vector of length length(parts) giving a label per part in order. Labels must be unique across parts (a label may not repeat another part's label or raw name). Stored on the object as a complete named vector keyed by every part; NULL (default) means the raw part names are used throughout.

units

Optional unit label for the closure scale, a single string such as "min/day" for a 1440-minute day. The print methods show it verbatim after the closure and after values reported on that scale. It also appears in the summary.compD() and summary.realloc() publication tables (pub_ready()). NULL (default) shows no unit.

impute_method

Zero-imputation method, passed to comp_impute() (ignored when the composition has no zeroes). Defaults to "lrEM" (log-ratio EM); see comp_impute() for the alternatives.

detect_outliers

Single logical; flag compositional outliers (comp_outliers()) on the zero-free parts. Default FALSE.

outlier_args

A named list of further arguments for comp_outliers(), most usefully quantile (the chi-squared cutoff probability) or alpha (MCD's subset proportion). With detect_outliers = FALSE it is only checked to be a named list. With TRUE, a name that comp_outliers() does not accept is an error.

...

Additional arguments forwarded to comp_impute(), and from there to the chosen method. The most useful is dl, the per-part detection limit below which an imputed value must fall. By default declare_composition() derives it from each part's smallest observed positive value on the original scale. Override it with dl = <vector or matrix of limits>, or pass other method-specific controls such as lrEM()'s rob, tolerance or max.iter.

Value

An object of class compD: a list with elements

data_raw

The original input data (a tibble), unchanged, so it may still contain zeroes. With detect_outliers = TRUE it also carries three appended columns: .outlier_distance (the Mahalanobis distance in ILR coordinates), .outlier_limit (the cutoff, constant down the column) and .outlier (logical).

parts

The character vector of part names.

closure

The resolved numeric closure (always a positive number, even when the user supplied "percent" or "mean").

composition

The imputed, closed composition, a compositions::acomp() object, from which summary.compD() and plot.compD() compute everything they show.

parts_imputed

The zero-free parts on the original (pre-closure) scale, a tibble: the input values with any zeroes replaced by comp_impute(). It keeps each row's absolute total, which the include_total (Coenders T-space) covariate of comp_iv() requires.

imput_table

A tibble describing zero occurrence per part: part, n, n_zero, pct_zero, min_nonzero.

labels

Either NULL or a complete named character vector keyed by every part, giving the display label used in summaries and plots.

units

The units argument as given, or NULL.

impute_method

The impute_method argument, or NA_character_ when no part had a zero (the method was requested but never run). summary.compD() reports it as the method used.

Details

Compositional data carry only relative information, and a zero has no log-ratio. When zeroes are present, comp_impute() imputes them on the original (pre-closure) scale before compositions::acomp() closes the result. Every downstream description, plot and coordinate is computed from this imputed, closed composition. The zero-free values on the original scale keep each row's absolute total and are stored as parts_imputed for the include_total T-space covariate of comp_iv(). Without zeroes, no imputation is performed and parts_imputed equals the input parts.

Outlier flagging

With detect_outliers = TRUE, comp_outliers() runs on the zero-free parts after imputation, and its per-observation columns are appended to data_raw as .outlier_distance, .outlier_limit and .outlier. Rows are flagged and never dropped. Every field of the object keeps one entry per input observation, and data_raw, composition and parts_imputed stay row-aligned with the input and with each other.

Filtering is left to the caller. Dropping the flagged rows means declaring the composition again, which recomputes it (and closure = "mean") on the remaining rows. The .outlier columns must be dropped in the same step. declare_composition() writes them itself and stops with an error on any input that already carries them, whether or not detection is requested.

kept <- cd$data_raw |>
  dplyr::filter(!.outlier) |>
  dplyr::select(-dplyr::starts_with(".outlier"))

cd_kept <- declare_composition(kept, parts, closure = 1440)

References

Palarea-Albaladejo, J., & Martín-Fernández, J.A. (2015). zCompositions – R package for multivariate imputation of left-censored data under a compositional approach. Chemometrics and Intelligent Laboratory Systems, 143, 85-96. doi:10.1016/j.chemolab.2015.02.019

See also

summary.compD() and plot.compD() to describe and visualize the object; comp_impute() and comp_outliers() for the zero-imputation and outlier-detection steps on their own; comp_iv() to model it as a predictor of an outcome.

Other declare and describe composition: comp_impute(), comp_outliers(), plot.compD(), summary.compD()

Examples

cd <- declare_composition(
  timeuse,
  parts = c("MVPA", "LPA", "SB", "SPT"),
  closure = 1440,
  units = "min/day"
)
cd$imput_table
#> # A tibble: 4 × 5
#>   part      n n_zero pct_zero min_nonzero
#>   <chr> <int>  <int>    <dbl>       <dbl>
#> 1 MVPA    300      0        0         0.1
#> 2 LPA     300      0        0        51.8
#> 3 SB      300      0        0       316. 
#> 4 SPT     300      0        0       240. 

set.seed(1)
flagged <- declare_composition(
  timeuse,
  parts = c("MVPA", "LPA", "SB", "SPT"),
  closure = 1440,
  detect_outliers = TRUE
)
sum(flagged$data_raw$.outlier)
#> [1] 14
